chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from his father, from some of his companions, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān; and al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ḥammād, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah and al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, all together from Ibn Sinān, who said:
I heard Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام saying: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said:

In mistaken killing resembling intentional killing, it is that one kills with a whip, a stick, or a stone. Indeed, the diyah for that is made heavier, and it is one hundred camels: among them forty khalifah camels, ranging between a thaniyyah and a bāzil in its year, thirty ḥiqqah, and thirty bint labūn. As for mistake, in it there are thirty ḥiqqah, thirty bint labūn, twenty bint makhāḍ, and twenty male ibn labūn from the camels. The value of each camel is one hundred and twenty dirhams or ten dīnārs, and from sheep, the value of each aged camel from the camels is twenty sheep.

key_terms.الْإِبِلِ: camels, the principal unit used here for assessing diyah
key_terms.بِنْتَ لَبُونٍ: a female camel of a defined age category used in diyah assessment
key_terms.بِنْتَ مَخَاضٍ: a younger female camel category used in diyah assessment
key_terms.حِقَّةً: a specified age category of camel used in diyah assessment
key_terms.دَنَانِيرَ: gold dinars as a monetary valuation of the diyah
key_terms.دِيَةَ: blood money or legal compensation for homicide
key_terms.شِبْهِ الْعَمْدِ: quasi-intentional killing, resembling deliberate action without full intent to kill

ai.seo_question: What is the diyah for accidental killing and quasi-intentional killing in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings for diyah in cases of accidental killing and quasi-intentional killing. It distinguishes between levels of liability and specifies the composition and monetary valuation of the compensation in camels, dīnārs, dirhams, and sheep.
